steps: Start with native Arbitrum USDC and buy discounted exact-contract USDC.e in an actually available AMM pool.
Redeem the USDC.e through its verified canonical gateway to the exact Ethereum native-USDC contract after the required dispute process.
Use the documented native-USDC CCTP Ethereum-to-Arbitrum rail to return native Arbitrum USDC and restore the starting asset.
hypothetical_cycle.who_pays: A seller willing to discount a delayed/bridge-backed claim for immediacy; not a stablecoin issuer paying free yield.
hypothetical_cycle.repeatability: Requires recurring real discounted flow, sufficient pool depth, functioning and backed redemption, and a net margin above all capital/time and execution costs. None was measured.
hypothetical_cycle.economic_net_identity: native_USDC_returned - native_USDC_spent - all_USD_gas_and_relay_costs - actual_financing_costs - allocated_operating_costs - realized_losses
hypothetical_cycle.benchmark_treatment: Any exposure-weighted benchmark excess is separate from economic net; do not subtract the same funding or inventory cost twice.
cheapest_falsifiers: No supported exact USDC.e gateway mapping or insufficient redeemable parent-chain backing.
No executable native-USDC/USDC.e discount at the intended size after AMM fee/slippage.
Discount smaller than measured canonical claim gas plus CCTP/relay costs and capital locked across the actual dispute interval.
Paused/denied transfer, missing capacity or user-ineligible access breaks the cycle.
Apparent par quote refers to a different token contract, wrapped output or conditional issuer access.
